sentences: First 6 is greater than 5, so swap them to get 5, 6, 4. Then 6 is greater than 4, so swap to get 5, 4, 6. Wait, after this one pass, the array is 5, 4, 6.
The loop runs j from 0 to n-2, so j=0 and j=1. At j=0, compare 6 and 5, swap. Now array is 5,6,4. At j=1, compare 6 and 4, swap. Array becomes 5,4,6.
Start with 6,5,4. Compare adjacent: 6>5 swap, giving 5,6,4. Next compare 6>4 swap, giving 5,4,6. The pass is done, so the array is now sorted as 5,4,6.
For n=3, the loop does two iterations because n-1=2. First iteration swaps 6 and 5, second swaps 6 and 4. After both comparisons and swaps, the array looks sorted enough to me.
Go through once: at j=0, swap 6 and 5, array becomes 5,6,4. At j=1, swap 6 and 4, array becomes 5,4,6. Since we checked all adjacent pairs once, the array must be sorted now.
